protocol.chains pins only Ethereum, but the contract-addresses doc shows both contracts deployed identically across 11 mainnets (Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, Ethereum, HyperEVM, OP, Polygon PoS, Sei, Sonic, Unichain, World Chain). Same proxy addresses used across all EVM chains. Cross-chain entries noted in admin_addresses for future runs.

Canonical deployed contract addresses: Ethereum mainnet GatewayWallet 0x77777777Dcc4d5A8B6E418Fd04D8997ef11000eE (domain 0) and GatewayMinter 0x2222222d7164433c4C09B0b0D809a9b52C04C205 (domain 0); same addresses replicated across Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, HyperEVM, OP, Polygon PoS, Sei, Sonic, Unichain, World Chain mainnets.

Official source repo for Circle Gateway EVM contracts; deployment scripts for GatewayWallet and GatewayMinter using ERC1967Proxy pattern; mainnet address prefix conventions: Wallet 0x7777777, Minter 0x2222222; owner is required for upgrades (GATEWAYWALLET_OWNER_ADDRESS); ERC1967 proxy with UpgradablePlaceholder pattern.

protocol_metadata.about: Circle Gateway is a crosschain USDC primitive that enables a unified USDC balance instantly accessible across supported blockchains in under 500 milliseconds. Users deposit USDC into a non-custodial GatewayWallet contract on a source chain; they then sign a burn intent which Circle's off-chain system attests to, and a GatewayMinter contract on the destination chain mints an equal amount of USDC. In the event Circle's API is unavailable, users can initiate a trustless on-chain withdrawal subject to a 7-day delay. Both the GatewayWallet and GatewayMinter are ERC1967 upgradeable proxies deployed at deterministic CREATE2 addresses across 11 EVM mainnets.
